article.title: Why Feature Stores Need Point-in-Time Correctness

paragraphs.en:
Machine-learning models are often trained with historical features: account balance, recent purchases, number of visits, customer status, or events in the previous thirty days. A subtle problem appears when the training pipeline uses information that was not actually available at the moment the prediction would have been made. This is data leakage, and point-in-time correctness is one of the main defenses against it.

Suppose a model predicts on January 10 whether a customer will purchase during the next month. The training row for January 10 must use only information known by January 10. If a feature table is rebuilt later and contains the customer’s status as of February, a simple join by customer ID may accidentally attach future information to the January row.

The model can then look excellent in offline evaluation because it is indirectly seeing the answer. In production, that future information does not exist, so performance drops. The problem is especially dangerous because the feature itself may look perfectly reasonable. The error is in time alignment, not necessarily in the column name.

A point-in-time join adds time to the matching rule. For each training event, the pipeline retrieves the latest valid feature value at or before the prediction timestamp, rather than the latest value available today. Historical feature stores often keep multiple versions of a customer’s features so that this lookup can be reproduced.

Event time and processing time also need careful distinction. A transaction may occur on Monday but arrive in the warehouse on Wednesday. If the production model on Tuesday could not have seen it, a faithful training dataset should not pretend that it could. The correct rule depends on the real information availability of the system.

Point-in-time correctness should be tested, not assumed. Teams can create checks that reject feature records with timestamps after the prediction time, review suspiciously predictive features, and reproduce selected historical predictions from raw events. Feature definitions should document both the observation window and any data-arrival delay.

This matters beyond machine learning. Customer segmentation, campaign eligibility, fraud analysis, and operational dashboards can all become misleading when later information is joined back into an earlier decision context. A campaign model, for example, must not use a customer status that was updated only after the campaign response occurred.

Teams should also distinguish a feature's business timestamp from the timestamp when a database row was updated. Backfills and corrections can rewrite historical tables. Without versioning, the table visible today may not represent what was visible to the model months ago.

The principle is simple: when reconstructing the past, use only what the system could have known at that time. A feature store is valuable not merely because it centralizes reusable features, but because it can make this temporal rule consistent across training and serving. Without point-in-time correctness, historical data can quietly give a model knowledge from the future and produce an evaluation that cannot be reproduced in real operation.
paragraphs.zh:
模型訓練時如果用了 prediction timestamp 之後才知道的資訊，就會發生 data leakage。Point-in-time correctness 要求每一筆歷史 training row 只能取得當時真正可用的 feature。

例如 1 月 10 日做預測，就不能把 2 月更新的 customer status join 回 1 月資料。Point-in-time join 會依時間取 prediction 時點以前最近的有效值，而不是今天資料表中的 latest value。還要區分 event time 與 processing time：週一發生但週三才進 warehouse 的交易，週二的 production model 其實看不到。

因此 feature definition 應記錄 observation window、arrival delay、business timestamp 與版本資訊，並測試是否有 future timestamp。Backfill 也可能重寫歷史資料，所以「今天看到的歷史表」不一定等於「當時模型真正看到的資料」。
paragraphs.ja:
モデル学習で予測時点より後に判明した情報を使うと data leakage が発生します。Point-in-time correctness とは、各 training row がその予測時点で実際に利用可能だった feature だけを参照するという原則です。

1月10日の予測に2月時点の customer status を結合してはいけません。Point-in-time join では、現在の最新値ではなく予測 timestamp 以前の最新有効値を取得します。また event time と processing time も区別します。月曜に発生して水曜に warehouse に到着した取引は、火曜の production model には見えていません。

Feature definition には observation window、data-arrival delay、business timestamp、version を記録し、future timestamp が混入していないか検証する必要があります。Backfill で履歴表が書き換わる場合もあるため、今日見える過去データが当時のモデル入力と同じとは限りません。
